key_insight: A three-stage framework and MoTok — a diffusion-based discrete motion tokenizer — bridge semantic planning and kinematic control by generating discrete semantic tokens with diffusion and then synthesizing high-fidelity continuous motion conditioned on those tokens.
problem_solved: Existing motion generation splits: continuous diffusion gives good kinematic realism but weak semantic conditioning, while discrete token models support semantics but lack fine-grained kinematic control. The paper solves how to combine strong semantic conditioning with precise kinematic synthesis in a unified pipeline.
method: Perception: extract condition features (e.g., text, action labels, sensors) into semantic representations.
Planning: MoTok — a diffusion-based discrete motion tokenizer that generates discrete semantic motion tokens, decoupling semantic planning from low-level motion details.
Control: diffusion-based motion synthesis that decodes tokens into continuous, physically plausible motion trajectories with strong kinematic fidelity.
impact: Provides a modular, interpretable pipeline enabling practitioners to plug in rich semantic conditions while retaining high-quality kinematics—useful for animation, robotics, and conditional motion generation research.
